## Story Goal

A logged-in customer, agent, or admin can change their own account password from the existing Settings page without contacting anyone. On success the new password is hashed with the same bcrypt cost the rest of the codebase uses, every **other** active refresh-token family for the user is revoked (forcing other devices to log back in), the caller's current session keeps working, and a best-effort "your password was changed" confirmation email is sent to the account's email on file. Available identically to all three roles from one shared endpoint and one shared UI section — no per-role branching.

Explicitly **not in scope**: forgot-password / logged-out flow (Story 65), admin-resets-another-user's-password, rate-limiting.

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Add a shared "revoke all other refresh families" helper

**File: `backend/src/utils/refreshToken.ts`**

Add a helper (or, if you prefer, put it next to the other family functions in `backend/src/routes/auth.routes.ts` — but export it so Story 65 can reuse it):

```ts
import { RefreshFamily } from "../models/RefreshFamily";

/**
 * Revoke every active RefreshFamily for a user, optionally exempting the
 * caller's current familyId so they stay logged in on this device.
 * Called by Story 64 (change password) and Story 65 (reset password).
 */
export async function revokeAllRefreshFamiliesForUser(
  userId: string,
  exemptFamilyId: string | null,
): Promise<number> {
  const filter: Record<string, unknown> = { userId, revoked: false };
  if (exemptFamilyId) filter.familyId = { $ne: exemptFamilyId };
  const result = await RefreshFamily.updateMany(filter, { $set: { revoked: true } });
  return result.modifiedCount ?? 0;
}
```

The `userId` field on `RefreshFamily` is confirmed via the existing revoke pattern in `auth.routes.ts:294`, which reads `family.userId`.

### 2 — Add validation schema

**File: `backend/src/validation/me.schema.ts`**

Add the schema next to the existing `me` schemas:

**Reuse, don't hand-roll:** `backend/src/validation/common.ts` already exports `requiredString(message)` and `passwordSchema(requiredMessage)` (the exact ≥8-char rule, `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8`) — `backend/src/validation/auth.schema.ts`'s `registerBodySchema` builds on these. Import and reuse them instead of re-declaring `z.string().min(8, ...)`:

```ts
import { requiredString, passwordSchema } from "./common";

export const changePasswordSchema = z.object({
  currentPassword: requiredString("currentPassword is required"),
  newPassword: passwordSchema("newPassword is required"),
  // Raw refresh-token value forwarded by the frontend Server Action (read
  // from its own REFRESH_COOKIE), used only to identify which
  // RefreshFamily is the caller's current session so it can be exempted
  // from the bulk revoke below — optional because a caller with no
  // active refresh session (e.g. access-token-only) can still change
  // their password, they just lose every session including this one.
  refreshToken: z.string().optional(),
});
```

Do **not** enforce "differs from current" here — that requires the DB row and is enforced in the handler.

### 3 — Add the endpoint

**File: `backend/src/routes/me.routes.ts`**

Add a `PATCH /password` handler between the existing `PATCH /contact` handler (line 423) and the email-confirmation routes. Skeleton:

**Correction to this plan's original draft:** there is no `validate`/`validateBody` middleware wired into any `me.routes.ts` handler today — `/availability` and `/contact` both parse their own schema inline with `.safeParse(req.body ?? {})` and return 400 themselves (see `me.routes.ts` lines ~76-80 and ~425). `backend/src/middleware/validate.ts` does export a `validateBody`/`validateParams` pair, but it's unused elsewhere in this router, so follow the router's own established convention rather than introducing the first use of that middleware here:

```ts
router.patch(
  "/password",
  requireAuth,
  async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
    const parsed = changePasswordSchema.safeParse(req.body ?? {});
    if (!parsed.success) {
      res.status(400).json({ error: parsed.error.issues[0]?.message ?? "Invalid request" });
      return;
    }
    const { currentPassword, newPassword, refreshToken } = parsed.data;
    const userId = req.user!.id;

    const user = await User.findById(userId);
    if (!user) {
      res.status(404).json({ error: "user not found" });
      return;
    }
    if (!user.isActive) {
      res.status(403).json({ error: "account is not active" });
      return;
    }

    const currentOk = await bcrypt.compare(currentPassword, user.passwordHash);
    if (!currentOk) {
      res.status(400).json({
        error: "current password is incorrect",
        fieldErrors: { currentPassword: "current password is incorrect" },
      });
      return;
    }

    const sameAsCurrent = await bcrypt.compare(newPassword, user.passwordHash);
    if (sameAsCurrent) {
      res.status(400).json({
        error: "new password must differ from current password",
        fieldErrors: { newPassword: "new password must differ from current password" },
      });
      return;
    }

    user.passwordHash = await bcrypt.hash(newPassword, BCRYPT_SALT_ROUNDS);
    await user.save();

    // Identify the caller's current session to exempt it from bulk revoke.
    // refreshToken is NOT a cookie the backend can read directly — it's the
    // raw value the frontend Server Action forwards from its own
    // REFRESH_COOKIE, same convention as POST /auth/refresh and
    // POST /auth/logout's req.body.refreshToken.
    const currentFamilyId = typeof refreshToken === "string" ? parseFamilyId(refreshToken) : null;
    await revokeAllRefreshFamiliesForUser(userId, currentFamilyId);

    // Best-effort confirmation email — must not roll back the password change.
    // NOTE: renderEmailHtml's REAL signature (backend/src/services/email.service.ts:46)
    // is `{ heading, bodyHtml, ctaText, ctaUrl }`, not `{ title, body }` — this
    // plan's earlier draft cited the wrong shape; corrected below.
    try {
      const loginUrl = `${process.env.CLIENT_ORIGIN || "http://localhost:3000"}/login`;
      await sendEmail({
        to: user.email,
        subject: "Your password was changed",
        text: `Your password was changed. If this wasn't you, contact support immediately.\n\nSign in: ${loginUrl}`,
        html: renderEmailHtml({
          heading: "Your password was changed",
          bodyHtml: `<p>Your account password was just changed.</p><p>If you did not do this, contact support immediately.</p>`,
          ctaText: "Sign in",
          ctaUrl: loginUrl,
        }),
      });
    } catch (err) {
      console.warn("[me/password] confirmation email failed", err);
    }

    await recordAuditLog({
      actor: userId,
      action: "password_changed",
      targetType: "User",
      targetId: userId,
      ipAddress: req.ip,
    });

    res.status(200).json({ ok: true });
  },
);
```

Imports to add to `me.routes.ts` (some already present):

- `bcrypt` from `"bcryptjs"` (**correction:** this codebase uses the `bcryptjs` package everywhere, not `bcrypt` — see `backend/src/routes/auth.routes.ts:2`'s `import bcrypt from "bcryptjs"`).
- `BCRYPT_SALT_ROUNDS` — either import from `../routes/auth.routes` (export it if not already exported) **or** re-declare `const BCRYPT_SALT_ROUNDS = 10;` local to this file to match the pattern already used in `auth.routes.ts`, `admin.routes.ts`, `customer.routes.ts`. Reuse via export is preferred to avoid the constant drifting.
- `parseFamilyId` from `"../utils/refreshToken"`.
- `revokeAllRefreshFamiliesForUser` from `"../utils/refreshToken"`.
- `changePasswordSchema` from `"../validation/me.schema"`.

No `cookie-parser` dependency, no `req.cookies` access, nothing to wire on the backend for this. **File: `backend/src/routes/auth.routes.ts` line 22**

Change `const BCRYPT_SALT_ROUNDS = 10;` to `export const BCRYPT_SALT_ROUNDS = 10;` so `me.routes.ts` can reuse it without duplicating the constant. ### 6 — Register `password_changed` as a real audit action

**File: `backend/src/models/AuditLog.ts`**

`recordAuditLog`'s `action` field is **not** a free string — it's a restricted union (`AuditAction`, ~line 22) backed by a Mongoose `enum: AUDIT_ACTIONS` (line 190), where `AUDIT_ACTIONS` is derived from `Object.keys(AUDIT_ACTION_CATEGORY)` (line 136). Calling `recordAuditLog({ action: "password_changed", ... })` without registering it here will fail Mongoose schema validation at runtime (not just a TS error). Add it in both places, under the `// auth` grouping:

```ts
// in the AuditAction union, alongside login_success/login_failed/logout/customer_registered:
| "password_changed"
```

```ts
// in AUDIT_ACTION_CATEGORY, alongside the other auth entries:
password_changed: "auth",
```

If Story 65 (forgot password) is implemented after this story and also needs `password_reset`, it adds its own entry the same way — don't let one story's edit here clobber the other's; both are additive.

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — Add the Server Action

**File: `frontend/app/settings/actions.ts`**

Add next to `updatePhone` / `updateEmail`:

```ts
const changePasswordSchema = z
  .object({
    currentPassword: z.string().min(1, "Current password is required"),
    newPassword: z.string().min(8, "Password must be at least 8 characters"),
    confirmNewPassword: z.string().min(1, "Confirm your new password"),
  })
  .refine((v) => v.newPassword === v.confirmNewPassword, {
    path: ["confirmNewPassword"],
    message: "Passwords do not match",
  })
  .refine((v) => v.currentPassword !== v.newPassword, {
    path: ["newPassword"],
    message: "New password must differ from current password",
  });

export interface ChangePasswordActionState {
  ok?: boolean;
  error?: string;
  fieldErrors?: Partial<Record<"currentPassword" | "newPassword" | "confirmNewPassword", string>>;
}

export async function changePassword(
  _prev: ChangePasswordActionState,
  formData: FormData,
): Promise<ChangePasswordActionState> {
  const parsed = changePasswordSchema.safeParse({
    currentPassword: formData.get("currentPassword"),
    newPassword: formData.get("newPassword"),
    confirmNewPassword: formData.get("confirmNewPassword"),
  });
  if (!parsed.success) {
    const fieldErrors: ChangePasswordActionState["fieldErrors"] = {};
    for (const issue of parsed.error.issues) {
      const key = issue.path[0] as keyof NonNullable<ChangePasswordActionState["fieldErrors"]>;
      if (key && !fieldErrors[key]) fieldErrors[key] = issue.message;
    }
    return { error: "Please fix the errors below", fieldErrors };
  }

  // Call backend PATCH /api/v1/me/password using the same bearer-token +
  // one-retry-on-401 pattern callContactApi (line 20) already implements
  // for updatePhone/updateEmail — but this call ALSO needs the raw
  // REFRESH_COOKIE value forwarded as `refreshToken` in the body, which
  // callContactApi has no reason to do today. Do not silently reuse
  // callContactApi as-is; either extend it with an optional
  // `includeRefreshToken` flag or add a sibling helper
  // (`callChangePasswordApi`) that additionally does:
  //
  //   const cookieStore = await cookies();
  //   const refreshToken = cookieStore.get(REFRESH_COOKIE)?.value;
  //
  // and includes `refreshToken` (may be undefined) in the JSON body sent
  // to `PATCH /api/v1/me/password`, alongside currentPassword/newPassword
  // (never confirmNewPassword — that's client-side-only). Map a 400
  // response's `fieldErrors` into ChangePasswordActionState.fieldErrors;
  // on success return `{ ok: true }` (no error/fieldErrors).
  // ...
}
```

Follow the bearer-token + one-retry-on-401 shape `callContactApi` already implements — do not reinvent that part. Additionally import `REFRESH_COOKIE` from `@/lib/auth` (already imports `SESSION_COOKIE` from there) to read the refresh cookie described above. Do **not** add `"use server"` at file level — this file already carries the correct directive since `updatePhone`/`updateEmail` are Server Actions consumed by the Client Component `SettingsForm.tsx`.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Wrong current password** — `bcrypt.compare` returns false. Handler responds `400` with `fieldErrors.currentPassword`. No enumeration concern (caller is already authenticated). Enforced in the handler at Task 3.
- **New password identical to current** — second `bcrypt.compare` returns true; handler responds `400` with `fieldErrors.newPassword`. Enforced server-side; the frontend zod refine is a UX shortcut only and must not be trusted.
- **New password shorter than 8 chars** — rejected by `changePasswordSchema.safeParse` inline in the handler (same convention as `/availability`'s `availabilityBodySchema.safeParse`). Same rule as `frontend/app/register/actions.ts:12`.
- **Confirm-new-password mismatch** — client-only concern, enforced by the frontend zod refine. Backend does not receive `confirmNewPassword`.
- **Deactivated account (`isActive === false`)** — reject with `403`, do not rotate. Mirrors the `isActiveAccount` check pattern at `me.routes.ts:188`.
- **Missing/invalid `refreshToken` body field** — `parseFamilyId` returns `null`; the revoke call then revokes **all** active families for the user (including this session). This is acceptable: if we can't identify the current family, safest behavior is to force a fresh login everywhere. Document this in a code comment.
- **Email send fails** — wrapped in try/catch; logged via `console.warn`. Password change already committed to Mongo; must not throw or roll back. Explicit AC.
- **Concurrent change-password requests from the same user** — last write wins on `passwordHash`; both requests succeed independently. Not a correctness issue for this story.
- **Unicode passwords** — bcrypt handles UTF-8 bytes; no special handling. Same behavior as sign-up/login.
- **User row disappears between `findById` and `save`** — `save()` will throw; error handler middleware returns 500. Acceptable — self-scoped, race is essentially impossible outside of admin-deletes-me flows.
- **`refreshToken` omitted by an older/misbehaving client** — `changePasswordSchema` marks it optional precisely so this can't 400 the request; falls into the "missing" case above.

## Test Plan

1. **Unit — validation schema** in `backend/tests/validation/me.schema.test.ts` (create if absent) or inline in the routes test: `changePasswordSchema` rejects short passwords, missing fields, and passes on valid input.
2. **Integration — `PATCH /api/v1/me/password`** in `backend/tests/routes/me.routes.test.ts`, following the fixture style used for `PATCH /me/availability` and `PATCH /me/contact`:
   - happy path: valid current + valid new → `200 { ok: true }`, `User.passwordHash` changed, `bcrypt.compare(newPassword, hash)` true.
   - wrong current password → `400`, `fieldErrors.currentPassword` present, hash unchanged.
   - new password `< 8` chars → `400` (validate middleware).
   - new password identical to current → `400`, `fieldErrors.newPassword` present.
   - deactivated account → `403`.
   - unauthenticated (no JWT) → `401` (via `requireAuth`).
3. **Integration — RefreshFamily revocation:**
   - Seed the user with 3 active families (matching real login shape). Call the endpoint with body `refreshToken` set to family A's raw token → after the call, family A is still `revoked: false`; families B and C are `revoked: true`.
   - Call with `refreshToken` omitted → all three families are `revoked: true`.
4. **Integration — email best-effort:** mock `sendEmail` to throw; call the endpoint → responds `200`, password still changed, warning logged. Mirrors the "must not roll back" AC.
5. **Integration — audit log:** assert `recordAuditLog` is called with `action: "password_changed"`, `actor === targetId === userId`, no plaintext in metadata.
6. **Frontend smoke** (manual, no new automated frontend test unless project already has one for `SettingsForm`): open `/settings` as customer/agent/admin, submit change-password with each failure case and success case, confirm field errors render and success banner appears.

## Migration / Rollback

- No schema migration. `RefreshFamily.revoked` already exists.
- Rollback: revert the `me.routes.ts` handler, `me.schema.ts` addition, `refreshToken.ts` helper, `SettingsForm.tsx`/`settings/actions.ts` changes, and the two i18n JSON diffs. No data cleanup required (audit-log rows for `password_changed` are harmless left behind).
- Half-applied state (backend deployed, frontend not): endpoint exists but is unreachable from UI — safe.
- Half-applied state (frontend deployed, backend not): Server Action will fail with 404 from backend; users see the generic error banner — safe.

- [x] `PATCH /api/v1/me/password` handler added in `backend/src/routes/me.routes.ts`, gated by `requireAuth` only.
- [x] Handler rejects wrong current password with a clear field-level error, distinct from any "not found" case.
- [x] Handler rejects `newPassword < 8` chars via `changePasswordSchema` in `backend/src/validation/me.schema.ts`, matching `frontend/app/register/actions.ts:12`'s rule.
- [x] Handler rejects new-password-equals-current via `bcrypt.compare`, not by re-deriving plaintext.
- [x] On success, `User.passwordHash` is re-hashed via `bcrypt.hash(newPassword, BCRYPT_SALT_ROUNDS)`.
- [x] On success, every other active `RefreshFamily` for the user is `revoked: true`; the caller's current family (identified via `parseFamilyId(req.body.refreshToken)`, forwarded by the frontend Server Action from its own `REFRESH_COOKIE`) is **not** revoked.
- [x] `revokeAllRefreshFamiliesForUser(userId, exemptFamilyId)` exported from `backend/src/utils/refreshToken.ts` so Story 65 can reuse it.
- [x] On success, `sendEmail` fires a "Your password was changed" notification via `renderEmailHtml`; a failure to send is logged but does not roll back the password change.
- [x] The notification email never contains the new password (plaintext or hashed).
- [x] `"password_changed"` added to `AuditAction` and `AUDIT_ACTION_CATEGORY` in `backend/src/models/AuditLog.ts` (category `"auth"`) — required before `recordAuditLog` can use it without a schema-validation failure.
- [x] `recordAuditLog({ action: "password_changed", actor: userId, targetType: "User", targetId: userId })` is recorded; no password material in metadata.
- [x] Endpoint works identically for `customer`, `agent`, and `admin` roles (no role branch in code).
- [x] `frontend/app/settings/SettingsForm.tsx` renders a "Change password" section with three controlled `<PasswordInput>` fields (`currentPassword`, `newPassword`, `confirmNewPassword`), never `defaultValue`.
- [x] `frontend/app/settings/actions.ts` exports `changePassword` Server Action + `ChangePasswordActionState`; zod-validated; per-field errors surfaced.
- [x] Field-level error rendering matches the pattern in `frontend/app/login/LoginForm.tsx`.
- [x] `frontend/messages/en.json` and `frontend/messages/ar.json` both updated with the new `settings.changePassword.*` keys in the same change.
- [x] Tests in `backend/tests/routes/me.routes.test.ts` cover: happy path, wrong current password, short new password, same-as-current, deactivated account, unauthenticated, RefreshFamily revoke (with and without current-family exemption), email-send failure is swallowed, audit log recorded.
- [x] `cd backend && npm run build && npm test` clean; `cd frontend && npm run build` clean.
